title: 🏛️ Architecture — Layers
help: A one-screen index of how AgentCase is built today: the
that shows the numbers are still the legacy numbers. One or two lines each, for orientation rather than depth.
Each layer may only import from the layers below it, and ESLint fails the build when it does not. That is what keeps the arithmetic in one place (the
layer), the writes in one place (the commands in
) and the screens free of business formulas. Because every business edit is a command, undo, redo, multi-tab sync and the audit log work for every input without any screen having to implement them.

genuinely computes: it owns the canonical payback and NPV and drives every horizon from 1 to 10 years. The command bus, the persistence adapters and the audit ring observe and coordinate; they never change a euro.

Anyone who has to answer "is this a spreadsheet with a UI, or an actual model?", and anyone about to change the code who needs to know which layer they are standing in. Users who know the legacy vocabulary (BUS, APP_STATE, PM, DEP, AUDIT, TIME) will find the mapping to today's mechanisms in the table at the bottom.

This is the overview. For modules, key functions, the data flow of one user action, the file formats, security, performance budgets, known gaps and a before / after table, use 🏛️ Architecture — Layers content. The repository document docs/ARCHITECTURE.md carries the same material. The version is shown in the top bar.
body: Quick index of how AgentCase is built: four code layers, the Time Engine, the command bus, the Portfolio layer, persistence, the View selector and the proof layer. For the full technical detail, see
Shell, zones, 86 sections and widgets. Reads the document through selector hooks and acts only through controllers. It may import ui, controllers, store and domain, but never the write path (
). No business formula and, in the portfolio and aggregate-view code, no financial sum (rule A8).
The only code that dispatches commands: one module per area, each business edit registered as a named command. It may import controllers, store and domain.
One Immer-based document store with history, the audit ring and the persistence adapters, plus the React selector hooks. It may import store and domain.

Every number the app shows: the calculation model, the Time Engine, economics, stress, verification checks and the Portfolio maths. No I/O, no DOM, no store; it imports domain only, so any figure is testable in Node.
keeps the import direction above; at most 150 lines per
; no raw HTML injection; the English-only guard test fails on French text; and the A8 rule forbids
sums in the portfolio and aggregate-view UI code.
▼ the domain is evaluated over time by ▼
Fits the adoption curve, evaluates it monthly and owns the
payback and NPV. Horizons of 1 to 10 years all flow from it; the annual view is a reduce over its months. The headline (net, ROI, payback, NPV) has one owner:
Every business edit is one named, undoable command. A single Immer
per dispatch feeds history (coalescing, batch), remote patches from other tabs and the audit ring.
A file is a portfolio: common values, 1 to 50 products and waves.
sums the Time Engine rows of the planned products on one calendar, with knowledge subsets, portfolio stress and an edit scope (all products or this product only).

JSON v1 for one case and portfolio v1 for a portfolio, the HTML snapshot, autosave in IndexedDB, multi-tab sync over BroadcastChannel, the parameters, results and cost-model Excel workbooks, and the HTML report.

The top-bar View (Portfolio / Wave / Product) applies to all 86 sections by kind: results follow it, inputs stay per product with a read-only roll-up, static and portfolio sections ignore it. This section and its companion are independent of the view.

Oracle fixtures recorded from the frozen legacy file, a register of intentional deviations, a large automated test suite, UI parity against the legacy styles, axe accessibility audits, end-to-end smoke tests and a performance budget.
Where a constant would otherwise be duplicated, it is held once and read live.
— 84 top-level keys in the default case; everything that persists.
— 257 commands, each with a label and an undo round trip test.
— 166 bindable outputs with canonical formats, used by the Board.
— 86 sections in 15 groups, with order, tag and view kind.
The domain is split into 18 calculation zones (
); each module is tagged with its zone and the module that owns a figure with
, so a number has one source. A dependency graph is generated from the imports (
) and shown in the section Dependencies;
uses it to run only the tests a change can reach, while the full suite stays mandatory before a merge or a release.
Command bus and audit ring; store listeners (autosave, broadcast) and React subscriptions
The store: one immutable document, every write a command
Persistence adapters: snapshot JSON, autosave, HTML snapshot, Excel, report
Derived selectors memoised on document identity (WeakMap); no runtime graph
Verification checks (Logic verification) and the audit log of commands
The Time Engine in domain/time, with the canonical payback and NPV
